# Requirements Quality Checklist: Link Management Web Application

**Purpose**: Broad requirements-quality review across this feature's highest-risk areas — security/auth, API/contract completeness, data model & cross-service consistency, and UX scenario coverage — at a standard rigor level, framed for a peer/PR reviewer.
**Created**: 2026-08-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) (see also [plan.md](../plan.md), [data-model.md](../data-model.md), [contracts/](../contracts/))

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Security & Authentication Requirements

- [x] CHK001 Are session validity/expiration requirements defined for the Google-authenticated session (e.g. how long a session lasts, whether/how it's refreshed)? [Gap] — resolved: 72-hour fixed session lifetime, see Spec §FR-018
- [x] CHK002 Are the specific conditions under which a request is treated as "authenticated" vs. "anonymous" (for FR-017's IP-vs-account keying) explicitly defined? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017] — resolved: the ambiguity is gone because the anonymous/IP-keyed branch was removed entirely (FR-017 is now account-keyed only, per Clarifications session 2026-08-17)
- [x] CHK003 Is the exact set of fields captured from the Google identity (beyond `google_subject_id`/email) specified, along with any additional PII-handling requirement? [Gap] — resolved: `google_subject_id` + `email` only, no additional fields/PII rule needed
- [x] CHK004 Are the "unsafe URL" criteria in FR-006 (structural checks + external reputation service) specific enough to be implemented and tested independently, without further interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006] — resolved: external reputation check removed (Clarifications 2026-08-17); FR-006 is now structural-only and unambiguous
- [x] CHK005 Is the ownership-check requirement (FR-010) stated consistently across every route it governs — update, delete, analytics, and QR? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010] — confirmed consistent
- [x] CHK006 Are rate-limit threshold values (request count, time window) required to be specified anywhere, or is that explicitly left as an implementation default? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-017] — resolved: MUST be configurable (env/config), not hardcoded (Clarifications 2026-08-17)
- [x] CHK007 Does the spec define what response a rate-limited request receives, distinct from an ownership-rejected or validation-rejected response? [Gap, Spec §FR-017] — resolved: FR-019 formalizes 400 (validation) / 403 (ownership) / 404 (not found) / 429 (rate limit) as distinct responses
- [x] CHK009 Is account/session compromise (e.g. a hijacked Google session) addressed by any requirement, or explicitly out of scope? [Gap] — resolved: explicitly out of scope, added to spec.md Assumptions

## API / Contract Completeness

- [x] CHK010 Are success and failure response bodies specified for every write route (create, update, delete), not just status codes? [Completeness, contracts/links.md] — resolved: shared "Response Body Conventions" added to contracts/links.md, referenced from analytics.md/qr.md
- [x] CHK011 Does the update route's contract reflect FR-017's rate-limiting requirement (create AND update), or does a gap remain between the clarified spec and the existing contract? [Conflict, Spec §FR-017 vs. contracts/links.md] — resolved earlier, before /speckit-tasks: contracts/links.md and research.md both updated
- [x] CHK012 Are the list route's (`GET /links`) requirements — pagination, ordering, maximum result size — specified, or left undefined? [Gap, contracts/links.md] — resolved: 100/page, newest-first, no separate total cap (FR-020)
- [x] CHK013 Are authorization-failure (403) responses specified consistently in shape/content across the links, analytics, and QR contracts? [Consistency, contracts/links.md, contracts/analytics.md, contracts/qr.md] — resolved by CHK010's shared Response Body Conventions
- [x] CHK014 Is the QR response's image format (SVG vs. PNG) a firm requirement, or explicitly left as an implementation choice? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, contracts/qr.md] — resolved: PNG, ≥512×512px, firm requirement (FR-012)
- [x] CHK015 Are requirements defined for what create/update return when multiple validation failures occur at once (e.g. malformed URL and a taken slug together)? [Gap, Edge Case] — resolved: all applicable failures reported at once (FR-021)
- [x] CHK016 Is a requirement/acceptance-criteria ID scheme (FR-xxx/SC-xxx) applied consistently across all contract documents so each can be traced back to the spec? [Traceability] — confirmed consistent

## Data Model & Cross-Service Consistency

- [x] CHK017 Is the Redis write-through key/value shape specified precisely enough (field names, types) to guarantee interoperability with `redirect/`'s independently-deployed cache reader? [Clarity, data-model.md] — resolved: key `link:{code}`, JSON string value (not a hash), ISO 8601 UTC timestamps; pinned identically in both features' data-model.md/research.md
- [x] CHK018 Are requirements defined for what happens to already-recorded `click_events` rows when their `code` is later deleted (retained, orphaned, or purged)? [Gap, Spec Edge Cases] — resolved: deleted via FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` (FR-022)
- [x] CHK019 Is the slug-uniqueness requirement (FR-007) explicit about case-sensitivity and allowed character set, or left undefined? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-007] — resolved: FR-007 is now a format check (lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens, 3–32 chars), not a uniqueness check at all — the slug/code redesign (Clarifications 2026-08-17) eliminated the uniqueness question entirely
- [x] CHK020 Are this feature's Short Link field requirements consistent with the fields `redirect/`'s own spec/data-model assume exist? [Consistency, data-model.md] — confirmed consistent, including the new `slug` field pinned identically on both sides
- [x] CHK021 Is a maximum/allowed length defined for a custom slug and for the destination URL? [Gap] — resolved for slug (3–32 chars, FR-007); destination URL length left as a reasonable implementation default (not scope-defining)
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for concurrent update attempts on the same link (e.g. two browser tabs saving conflicting changes)? [Gap, Edge Case] — resolved: last-write-wins, no conflict detection (spec.md Edge Cases)

## User Experience & Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK023 Are empty-state requirements defined for the link list view (a user with zero links)? [Gap, Coverage] — resolved: empty-state message with create-first-link CTA (spec.md Acceptance Scenario 2.5)
- [x] CHK024 Are loading/in-progress state requirements defined for the create/update actions and the analytics report? [Gap] — resolved: intentionally left as an implementation default (standard loading/disabled-submit pattern), not scope-defining
- [x] CHK025 Is the "expiration date in the past" edge case reflected as a testable functional requirement, or only present as narrative text under Edge Cases? [Traceability, Spec Edge Cases] — resolved: added FR-023 (was only narrative before); propagated to contracts/links.md and tasks.md T021/T029
- [x] CHK026 Are requirements defined for how a rejected or rate-limited creation attempt is communicated to the user, distinctly from other rejection reasons? [Gap, Spec §FR-017] — resolved by FR-019/CHK010's shared Response Body Conventions
- [x] CHK027 Are accessibility requirements specified for the create/manage/analytics/QR flows, beyond the constitution's English-only note? [Gap] — resolved: added FR-024, WCAG 2.1 AA best-effort target
- [x] CHK028 Is analytics time-bucketing — left to "reasonable defaults" per spec.md Assumptions — specified with enough detail for a reviewer to verify an implementation matches intent? [Ambiguity, Spec Assumptions] — resolved: fixed daily bucketing; retention window remains an implementation default

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK029 Is the "roughly a second" propagation target in SC-004 specific enough to be objectively measured, or does "roughly" leave room for divergent interpretations? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004] — resolved: quantified as p95 under 2 seconds; T015 now asserts it (also closes G1 from the earlier /speckit-analyze report)
- [x] CHK030 Are requirements defined for this application's own availability/health reporting (analogous to `redirect/`'s `/health` route), or is that intentionally out of scope? [Gap] — resolved: added FR-025, a separate public/unauthenticated human-readable status page alongside the JSON health endpoint (T040/T041)
- [x] CHK031 Are observability requirements (logging of rejected/rate-limited requests, an audit trail of link changes) specified anywhere? [Gap] — resolved: added FR-026, structured logging for all mutations and rejections (T046)

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK032 Is the assumption that this application solely owns the Postgres schema/migrations (research.md) checked against any conflicting expectation documented in `redirect/`'s own plan? [Assumption, research.md] — resolved: confirmed with the user, both sides' research.md updated from "assumed" to "confirmed," no conflict
- [x] CHK033 Is degraded behavior specified for the case where Google's OAuth service is unreachable during login? [Gap, Dependency] — resolved: standard error message, no fallback login method (spec.md Assumptions)

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
